evidence.text: The Phoenix opens a diary under the rattling weather vane. “A diary records what we observed. The weather has already volunteered to take all the blame.” Choose an earlier and a later actual radio reading from your notebook. Compare their SNR and distinguish a current observation from a historical one. No timer, ally or optional reward is needed.

The notebook supplies the actual source room, profile, attempt, configuration revision, signal in dBm, noise in dBm and SNR in dB for each reading. A later revision is a recorded sequence, not a wall-clock date or elapsed duration. A changed configuration makes the earlier record historical. Close the diary to change the radio controls or measure again, then reopen it.

You compared two actual Storm Observatory radio readings while preserving their recorded conditions and history. The later reading was current when the comparison was made; that is a historical learning achievement, not a promise that the link stays healthy. The optional radio explanation is unlocked. The diary changes no path, completes no main objective and does not establish a weather cause or throughput.

alternatives.label: Record the weather diary comparison
alternatives.explanation: Compare two actual recorded radio observations in their recorded order, with a current later sample. Correctly explain the SNR change, whether the current sample meets the supplied threshold and what the observations can prove. Historical passing evidence cannot prove the current link.

sourceClaims.section: Check Physical and Environmental Conditions; Run Connectivity Tests from the Web User Interface; Radio Settings; Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR)
sourceClaims.supportedClaim: Power, cable attachment, link indication, obstructions/range and connectivity tests are distinct observations; radio settings and noise affect diagnosis.
limitations: Product troubleshooting context, not universal SNR or throughput guarantees. Do not import configuration recommendations, channel legality, security or service success into the toy profile.

sourceClaims.supportedClaim: SNR is a signal-to-noise power ratio; its dB value is ten times the base-ten logarithm of that ratio.
limitations: For compatible power measurements with one reference, subtracting dBm yields dB. No universal acceptable threshold follows from this definition.

model.label: fictional-teaching-profile
model.scope: Optional comparison of actual R08/O08 radio observations using the reviewed T08, T09, B-RADIO-20 and B-RADIO-BELOW values and existing STATE01 freshness. The diary adds no propagation or weather model.
assumptions: Each selected sample is an actual notebook measurement from the reviewed R08/O08 radio path, with its original room, subjects, attempt, configuration revision and readings.

Both selected records contain viable-path and compatible-settings observations. The earlier record precedes the later configuration revision; the later record must match the current attempt and configuration and be explicitly nonstale.
The diary can be opened without an objective completion, party member, item or optional-activity prerequisite. A full comparison remains unavailable until the necessary actual measurements exist.
limitations: The supplied 20 dB inclusive minimum is a fictional threshold, not a universal radio or Wi-Fi requirement.
Recorded revision order does not establish a wall-clock timestamp, elapsed interval or weather causation. No rain attenuation, distance, gain or frequency formula is modeled.
An SNR comparison does not guarantee throughput, end-to-end service or a repaired path. Path viability and compatible settings remain independent requirements.
A correct diary diagnosis can describe a physically failed current link. It changes no equipment and does not complete O07 or O08.
Historical readings remain historical. A prediction or old passing sample cannot replace an actual current reading after a configuration change or Retry.

method.text: Choose two actual readings in recorded revision order. Read their SNR values in dB and compare the later value with the supplied inclusive 20 dB minimum. Keep the earlier record as history.

workedStep.text: Worked example: −65 dBm signal above −90 dBm noise gives 25 dB SNR. The same signal above −78 dBm noise gives 13 dB. The later SNR decreased by 12 dB and is below the fictional 20 dB minimum. The measurements alone do not identify a weather cause.

solution.text: For the 25 dB then 13 dB example, choose “SNR decreased”, “Below the supplied threshold” and “Use the current reading; cause and throughput remain unproven”. The old passing record is history. Other reviewed observation pairs may rise, stay equal or meet the threshold; compare your displayed readings. Help records assistance and earns the same optional depth.

observableOutcome: A correct comparison records the diary once and unlocks optional radio depth. It preserves both readings and their freshness. Wrong or missing answers receive an explanation and retry; missing actual evidence leaves full delivery unavailable. Exit stays at the captured Observatory location without consuming items or saving.
completionExplanation: “Excellent,” says the Phoenix. “The diary now contains observations instead of a weather forecast wearing a laboratory coat.” Your comparison is recorded and the deeper radio explanation is unlocked. The physical link still has the status shown by its latest actual reading; the diary has repaired nothing.
